tasks.title: Fix bulk discount boundary
tasks.detail: Customers ordering exactly 10 units of a line are not getting the 5% bulk discount. The business rule is: a line with quantity >= BULK_THRESHOLD (10) gets BULK_DISCOUNT. Fix invoice/pricing.py and add a regression test for quantity == 10 (expected line_total for 10 x 10.0 is 95.0).

tasks.title: Add CSV export
tasks.detail: Add invoice/export.py with to_csv(invoice) -> str. Header row: description,quantity,unit_price,category,line_total. One row per item with unit_price and line_total formatted with two decimals (e.g. 10.00). Last row: TOTAL,,,,<grand total incl. GST, two decimals>. Use the csv module. Add tests.
acceptance: last row starts with TOTAL and ends with grand_total

tasks.title: Refactor rounding into currency.round_money
tasks.detail: Rounding with round(x, 2) is duplicated across pricing.py and tax.py and uses banker's/float rounding (round(2.675, 2) == 2.67). Add round_money(amount: float) -> float to invoice/currency.py using decimal.Decimal(str(amount)) quantized to 0.01 with ROUND_HALF_UP, and replace every round(...) call in pricing.py and tax.py with round_money. Behaviour of existing tests must not change.
acceptance: no bare round( calls left in pricing.py/tax.py

tasks.title: Add input validation to LineItem
tasks.detail: LineItem accepts garbage today. Add __post_init__ validation raising ValueError when: description is empty/whitespace, quantity <= 0, unit_price < 0, or category is not one of the GST categories in invoice/tax.py (standard, essential, exempt). parse_items must raise ValueError whose message includes the 1-based data row number, e.g. 'row 2: quantity must be positive'. Avoid a circular import between models.py and tax.py.

tasks.title: Load supplier price list and sort it
tasks.detail: Our supplier publishes a price list page (saved at data/supplier_prices.html). Add invoice/catalog.py with load_catalog(path: str, sort_by: str = 'price', descending: bool = False) -> list[dict] that extracts the table rows as dicts with keys sku, item, category, price (float), stock (int), sorted by the sort_by column. Use only the standard library (html.parser). Use the scrape skill. Add tests.
acceptance: price is float, stock is int
sorted by price desc gives RC-01 first
